About this species: Lycium shawii is a spiny shrub or small tree of dry desert and semi-desert habitats. It grows in wadis, rocky slopes, sandy plains, and open shrublands, where it can tolerate heat, drought, and poor soils. Its spines and dense branching provide shelter for small animals and nesting sites for birds, while its fruits may contribute to desert food resources. The plant is a typical example of a drought-adapted woody shrub in Saharo-Arabian landscapes.
Geographical distribution: Sicilia to Kriti, Egypt to S. Africa and W. India.
